'''Blount''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who fought in the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Originally a member of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]], he defected to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] before [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] and joined [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]]. As a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]], he also served the Rebels as a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], [[Spy/Legends|spy]], and [[Scout/Legends|scout]], and by 4 ABY, he was considered a seasoned combat veteran. When the Alliance launched an [[Battle of Endor/Legends|assault]] on the Empire's unfinished [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] in that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], Blount joined the crew of the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], whose pilot, [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], led the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet's]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] contingent during the attack.

The Empire anticipated the strike, however, and when the Rebel [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] arrived at their target in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]], they found the [[Space station/Legends|station]] protected by a [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield]]. As they [[Starfighter combat/Legends|fended off]] attacking Imperial fighters, Blount served in a post aboard the ''Millennium Falcon''. The [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Space warfare/Legends|squared off]] against Imperial [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] during the battle, and eventually entered the incomplete [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] when a Rebel [[Endor strike team/Legends|strike team]] on the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]] below was able to blow up the station's [[Endor shield generator bunker|shield generator]]. Calrissian destroyed the Death Star's [[Reactor/Legends|reactor]] core; the station soon after exploded and the Rebels won the day.

==Biography==
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Blount served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] as a member of the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]].<ref name="CCG" /> Prior to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="Return of the Jedi">{{Film|VI}}</ref><ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> he defected to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], wherein he lent his skills to [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] and achieved the [[Rebel command insignia/Legends|rank]] of [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]]. Blount also served as a [[Spy/Legends|spy]] and a [[Scout/Legends|scout]],<ref name="CCG" /> and occasionally [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] a modified [[Z-95t Headhunter]] designated ''[[Tala 2]]'' for the Alliance's [[Tala Squadron]]. The reconnaissance [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] was used to monitor Imperial activity during Rebel [[Commando/Legends|commando]] operations. When piloting ''Tala 2'',<ref name="CCG 2">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Tala 2}}</ref> Blount was the [[Wingmate/Legends|wingman]] of [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]],<ref name="CCG" /> who flew in ''[[Tala 1]]''. Cracken's fighter was operationally assigned to support Rebel commandos serving under [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]],<ref name="CCG 3">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Tala 1}}</ref> an Alliance [[General/Legends|general]].<ref name="Return of the Jedi" />

At some point during his career, Blount visited [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]],<ref name="CCG" /> a [[Tibanna/Legends|tibanna]] [[Gas mine|gas mining]] colony that floated above the [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]] [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]].<ref name="The Empire Strikes Back">{{Film|V}}</ref> By 4 ABY, he had been involved in enough combat situations to be considered a seasoned veteran.<ref name="CCG" /> In that [[Standard year/Legends|year]],<ref name="NEC" /> he was with the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] in the [[Sullust system/Legends|Sullust system]] while an assault was planned on the Empire's [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]], a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] under construction in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] above the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]]. General [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] was selected to lead the starfighter contingent of the [[Navy/Legends|naval]] strike on the [[Space station/Legends|station]] from the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], and Blount joined the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter's]] crew as preparations were made throughout the [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]]. He stood in the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] with Calrissian, co-pilot [[Nien Nunb/Legends|Nien Nunb]], Airen Cracken, and another individual as the fleet entered [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] en route to Endor.<ref name="Return of the Jedi" />

[[File:Blountincockpit.jpg|thumb|left|325px|Lieutenant Blount stands in the cockpit of the ''Millennium Falcon'' just prior to the Battle of Endor.]]
The Rebels expected the [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield]] protecting the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] to be deactivated due to the efforts of a [[Endor strike team/Legends|strike team]] that had been dispatched to the moon and tasked with destroying the groundside [[Endor shield generator bunker|deflector shield generator]], but upon the fleet's arrival in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]], Calrissian discovered that the shield was still functional. The Empire had anticipated their arrival, and the fleet could do little save fend off attacking Imperial starfighters. Although Blount left the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} cockpit before the [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfighting]] began,<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> he continued to actively crew the freighter during the [[Space warfare/Legends|space battle]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|80|Blount, Lieutenant}}</ref> When the Death Star's [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]]&mdash;thought by the Alliance to be not yet operational&mdash;began to destroy Rebel [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]], the ''Millennium Falcon'' led the Rebels toward a nearby fleet of Imperial [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] to avoid the battlestation's powerful [[Laser/Legends|weapon]].<ref name="Return of the Jedi" />

The Alliance ships attacked the [[Destroyer/Legends|Destroyers]] at point-blank range,<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> and Calrissian at one point took the ''Millennium Falcon'' into an enemy [[Starship/Legends|vessel's]] [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] bay in an effort to dodge its [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]]. Explosions resulting from [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missiles]] fired by Nunb eventually covered the freighter's escape from the Destroyer's guns.<ref name="Gambler's Run">{{WEGCite|story=Gambler's Run|book=Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi}}</ref> The ''Millennium Falcon'' also aided in the destruction of the Empire's [[Pride of Tarlandia/Legends|main communications ship]], which neutralized the Empire's [[Jammer/Legends|jamming]] of the Alliance fleet. As a result,<ref name="novel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref> the Alliance was able to detect when the Rebel strike team finally destroyed the [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]]. Immediately thereafter, the ''Millennium Falcon'' and several other Rebel fighters entered the incomplete battlestation and made their way to its [[Reactor/Legends|reactor]] core.<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> Blount was aboard the freighter<ref name="CSWE" /> when its guns destroyed the core; [[Red Leader/Legends|Red Leader]] [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] also took out the station's power regulator from his [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighter]], and the two ships were able to escape from the Death Star mere [[Standard second|seconds]] before it was destroyed in a powerful explosion.<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> The Alliance won the battle and delivered a crippling blow to the Empire.<ref name="NEC" />

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Lieutenant_Blount_XWM.png|thumb|right|250px|Lieutenant Blount pilots a [[Z-95 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunter]].]]
During the Galactic Civil War, Blount defected from the Galactic Empire and joined the Rebel Alliance. He worked as an Intelligence agent in both organizations, and also served as a pilot, spy, and scout in the Alliance. He was skilled at flying and was considered to be a seasoned combat veteran. Blount had [[Color/Legends|green]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], fair skin,<ref name="CCG" /> and dark-blond [[Hair/Legends|hair]].<ref name="Fact File" />

==Equipment==
During the Battle of Endor, Blount wore standard-issue Alliance battledress, which included a protective [[Armor/Legends|helmet]], a thornproof jerkin, and an identity panel.<ref name="Fact File" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|He can be seen when the Falcon prepares itself to go make the jump to lightspeed. After this appearance he is not seen anymore, so I'd say we could presume he took place in the other quad gun, just like Cracken.|Tim Veekhoven, speculating on Lieutenant Blount's role during the Battle of Endor|<ref name="Sompeetalay">{{Blog|teekay-421|67/comments|The truth about Colonel Cracken & Lieutenant Blount}}</ref>}}
[[File:Fabulous80sHair-BluRay.jpg|thumb|left|350px|Blount mans one of the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} quad laser turrets in unused footage shot for ''Return of the Jedi''.]]
Lieutenant Blount first appeared in [[Richard Marquand]]'s [[1983]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], as a nameless background character standing in the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} cockpit during a single scene immediately prior to the Battle of Endor.<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> He was played by [[Trevor Butterfield]], who also played numerous other roles in both ''Return of the Jedi'' and in [[1980]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strike Back'']].<ref name="Butterfield interview">{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2012/10/trevor-butterfield-lieutenant-blount.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=Trevor Butterfield interview - Lieutenant Blount - Star Wars}}</ref> Additional footage was shot of both Blount and Airen Cracken rushing through the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} corridors alongside other Rebel crewmembers, and of the two of them manning the freighter's [[Quad laser cannon/Legends|quad laser cannons]].<ref name="Blu-ray">{{HomeVideoCite|set=Star Wars: The Complete Saga|scene=Battle of Endor: The Lost Rebels}}</ref> These scenes went unused in the film's final cut,<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> but the rough, unedited footage was later included in the [[2011]] ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' [[Wikipedia:Blu-ray Disc|Blu-ray]] release.<ref name="Blu-ray" />

The presence of two [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]] in the quad turrets during the battle was nevertheless canonized by ''[[Gambler's Run]]'', a short story originally published in the [[1990]] sourcebook ''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]'',<ref name="Gambler's Run" /> and Cracken has since been confirmed to be one of them.<ref name="Behind the Magic">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref><ref name="Rebellion Era Campaign Guide">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Although ''[[Star Wars]]'' author [[Tim Veekhoven]] surmised that Blount was likely the second gunner in a [[2006]] blog,<ref name="Sompeetalay" /> the [[Maintenance droid/Legends|maintenance droid]] [[MK-09/Legends|MK-09]] had in fact been named the other gunner in [[1999]].<ref name="X-wing strategy guide">[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> Therefore, Blount's specific role during the battle in [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Canon|continuity]] remains unknown.

The character was neither named nor given a backstory until [[2000]], for the [[Death Star II Limited]] expansion set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]].<ref name="CCG" /> A promotional photo of Blount and Cracken was later included in [[2002]]'s [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 30|Issue 30]] of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'', in an article discussing Rebel [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] present on Endor's surface during the Battle of Endor;<ref name="Fact File" /> however, Blount's presence aboard the ''Millennium Falcon'' during the battle has been confirmed by [[2008]]'s ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="CSWE" />

Neither Blount, Cracken, nor the Rebel navigator are present in the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} cockpit in the<ref name="Marvel">[[Return of the Jedi 3|''Return of the Jedi'' 3]]</ref> [[December 1]], 1983<ref name="Marvel date">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54532/star_wars_return_of_the_jedi_1983_3|text=Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (1983) #3}}</ref> [[Return of the Jedi 3|third issue]] of [[Marvel Comics]]' [[Star Wars (1977)|adaptation]] of the film,<ref name="Marvel" /> the [[September 1]], 1999<ref name="Manga date">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54536/star_wars_return_of_the_jedi_manga_1999_3|text=Star Wars: Return Of The Jedi Manga (1999) #3}}</ref> [[Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi 3|third issue]] of [[Dark Horse Comics]]' [[Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi|Manga adaptation]],<ref name="Manga">[[Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi 3|''Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi'' 3]]</ref> or in [[LucasArts]]' [[2006]] non-canon ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]''.<ref name="Lego">''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref> An alternate version of the battle occurs in the [[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi 3|third]] and [[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi 4|fourth]] issues of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] miniseries ''[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi]]'', in which the ''Millennium Falcon'' is crewed only by Calrissian, General [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], and the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]].<ref name="Infinities">[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi 3|''Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi'' 3]]</ref><ref name="Infinities4">[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi 4|''Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi'' 4]]</ref> Those issues were respectively released [[March 3]], 2004<ref name="Infinities 3 date">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/53973/star_wars_infinities_return_of_the_jedi_2003_3|text=Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi (2003) #3}}</ref> and [[March 31]] of the same year.<ref name="Infinities 4 date">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/53974/star_wars_infinities_return_of_the_jedi_2003_4|text=Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi (2003) #4}}</ref>

In [[1998]], [[Kenner Products]] released an "Endor Rebel Soldier" figure for their [[Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1995 toy line)|''Power of the Force'']] toy line. A variation of the packaging shows an image of Blount on Endor, conflicting with his [[in-universe]] role on the ''Millennium Falcon'' during the Battle of Endor. This article treats that image as an error. As Blount is not pictured in all versions of the figure's packaging, this article also avoids considering that figure as a confirmed representation of Blount.<ref name="Kenner figure">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1995 toy line)|pack=Endor Rebel Soldier|link=potf2endorsoldier.asp}}</ref>
